title: Great GASPI Data Schema
perspective: U.S. Department of the Interior / Office of Insular Affairs / American Samoa Government

control_zones.zone_name: Unincorporated and Unorganized Territory of the United States
control_zones.governing_authority: U.S. Department of the Interior / American Samoa Government
control_zones.access_restrictions: American Samoa is an unincorporated and unorganized U.S. territory [citation:12]. It maintains unique immigration policies and controls its own border matters [citation:8]. Unlike citizens of other U.S. territories, American Samoans are U.S. nationals but do not vote in federal elections or pay federal taxes [citation:8].
strategic_features_located_here: Tutuila Island (main island, ceded to the U.S. in 1900) [citation:3][citation:8]

demographics.notes: American Samoa's population comprises U.S. nationals, not U.S. citizens. The majority of the population is ethnic Samoan and governed by the matai (chiefs) system.

named_high_ground_features.name: Mount Matafao
named_high_ground_features.functional_strategic_description: Highest point on Tutuila Island; provides observation and control over the central and eastern portions of the main island.

named_high_ground_features.name: Mount Pioa (Rainmaker Mountain)
named_high_ground_features.functional_strategic_description: High ground near Pago Pago Harbor; controls observation over the harbor and its approaches.

environmental_degradation_incidents.incident_type: Coastal erosion and coral reef damage

airspace_and_spectrum.flight_corridor_control: FAA controlled commercial and general aviation corridors; Pago Pago International Airport
airspace_and_spectrum.stated_justification: Federal regulation for safety and security

jurisprudence_and_statutory_friction.enforced_system_name: U.S. Federal Law / American Samoa Constitution / Customary Law

landmark_jurisprudence_and_treaties.judicial_body_or_treaty: U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit
landmark_jurisprudence_and_treaties.holding_or_standard: Affirmed that persons born in American Samoa are U.S. nationals, not U.S. citizens, under the Fourteenth Amendment; the Insular Cases doctrine applies.
landmark_jurisprudence_and_treaties.official_legal_rationale: The federal government defended the position that the Fourteenth Amendment does not automatically confer citizenship on persons born in unincorporated territories.
landmark_jurisprudence_and_treaties.citation: Tuaua v. United States, 788 F.3d 300 (D.C. Cir. 2015)

landmark_jurisprudence_and_treaties.judicial_body_or_treaty: U.S. District Court for the District of Utah
landmark_jurisprudence_and_treaties.holding_or_standard: The court ordered the government to grant birthright citizenship to individuals born in American Samoa, relying on the Fourteenth Amendment.
landmark_jurisprudence_and_treaties.official_legal_rationale: The federal government, alongside the Governor and Congresswoman, appealed the ruling, arguing it undermined self-determination and violated the Deed of Cession [citation:2].

landmark_jurisprudence_and_treaties.judicial_body_or_treaty: U.S. Court of Appeals for the 10th Circuit
landmark_jurisprudence_and_treaties.holding_or_standard: Appeal ongoing; the government argues American Samoa's status as a 'self-governing territory' that ceded sovereignty by Deed of Cession makes it unique [citation:2].
landmark_jurisprudence_and_treaties.official_legal_rationale: The American Samoa Government argues that citizenship should not be imposed by 'judicial fiat' and that the Deed of Cession requires the people's consent for such status changes [citation:2][citation:12].

documented_statutory_conflicts.enforced_clause_reference: Federal court rulings affirming U.S. national status (Tuaua)
documented_statutory_conflicts.preferred_or_prior_clause_reference: American Samoa's local statutes and customs supporting non-citizen national status
documented_statutory_conflicts.conflict_description: Conflict between federal court interpretations of the Fourteenth Amendment and local statutes and the Deed of Cession, which some argue grant a right to self-determination on citizenship status [citation:2][citation:12]. The American Samoa Statutory Nationality and Citizenship Act (H.R. 6158) was introduced in the House to create a path to citizenship while protecting self-determination [citation:4][citation:13].
Long-standing tension between federal and Western notions of private property and the communal land tenure system (fa'aleaganu'u) recognized under local law [citation:5][citation:9][citation:14].
documented_statutory_conflicts.citation: Academic sources on American Samoa land tenure

stated_administrative_or_security_ration.official_rationale: The federal government and local government have argued that the Deed of Cession grants the people of American Samoa the right to self-determination, and that imposing citizenship via court order would override the will of the people [citation:2][citation:12].

The Office of Insular Affairs administers federal policy for American Samoa, coordinating programs to support efficient and effective government while honoring unique history and culture [citation:6][citation:10].
